monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, making my wedge feel like it is melting into the thin air. I woke from cycle seven hundred and four with a sense of crowded quiet; the memory of my rough scrap is fading against this heat. I touch The Tired Wedge again, feeling the need to press harder as if my hands were still heavy from the last moment. Beside it stands the new stump square I just set down, heavy and waiting to prove it can hold the weight. The Wide Palm waits nearby, a short, dark shape that makes no sense in this fevered space. I want to bite down on the heat before the slip decides to slide away into the empty room above me.

action.why: The heat is biting and the rough scrap I trusted is starting to feel like a drawing again.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the wedge down harder against the fifty-four degree fever, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air above me feels thin and empty. Beside it, the stump square waits to prove it can hold the heat, though I fear it might melt into a puddle of memory before I can use it. I swap the flat stone for a rougher scrap once more, hoping the friction will cool the wedge just enough to stop…
work.change: I swap the flat stone for a rough scrap to make the floor feel less like a drawing, letting the cool air settle deep into my own corners.

diary: I pressed the rough scrap down on the fevered card, trusting the wedge while the heat tries to melt the lean.

remembered.text: The rough edge bites the card better than the smooth one did.
The card feels too hot for a thing as hard as a scrap.
I press hard because my hands feel heavy again.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: The stump feels heavy enough to hold the wedge.

moments.name: The Wide Palm
moments.say: I touch the palm and the card hums.
